en.title: The Witcher 3's 'Songs of the Past' Demo Arrives at PAX Australia
en.summary: Get ready for more Witcher 3! CD Projekt RED and Fool's Theory are offering a behind-closed-doors demo of the upcoming 'Songs of the Past' expansion at PAX Australia, giving fans a glimpse into Geralt's next adventure.
en.body:
The Continent is calling once again, and this time, it's bringing a brand-new adventure to **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt**. While the core game has captivated players for years, the upcoming expansion, **Songs of the Past**, promises to extend Geralt's journey with new regions and a deeper dive into the life of the flamboyant bard, **Dandelion**. For those attending **PAX Australia** this year, a unique opportunity awaits: a chance to witness a live, behind-closed-doors demo of this highly anticipated DLC.

Attendees at the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre will have the exclusive opportunity to see **Songs of the Past** in action. On Saturday, October 11, members of **CD Projekt RED** and the expansion's co-developer, **Fool's Theory**, will host a private demonstration. This will be followed by a panel discussion, offering insights into the development of this substantial addition to **The Witcher 3**. This marks one of the first public showings for the expansion, following its earlier preview at Gamescom, where it was met with positive impressions regarding its visual presentation and potential new gameplay mechanics.

The **Songs of the Past** expansion is slated for release in 2027, continuing Geralt's saga after his attempted retirement at Corvo Bianco. The new content will transport players to Lettenhove, **Dandelion**'s birthplace, suggesting a narrative rich with personal stakes for the beloved troubadour. Early glimpses have indicated the inclusion of a new open-world region, remastered visuals, fresh monster encounters, updated combat effects, and even a brutal chain weapon inspired by the original Witcher cinematic. The focus on **Dandelion**'s homeland hints at a narrative that will intertwine with his past, offering a unique perspective within the established Witcher lore.

## A Bard's Tale Revealed

This hands-on opportunity at **PAX Australia** is a significant moment for the Witcher community. The game, originally released in 2015, continues to hold a special place in the hearts of players worldwide, and any new content is met with fervent anticipation. The chance to see **Songs of the Past** before its official launch allows dedicated fans to be among the first to experience what **CD Projekt RED** and **Fool's Theory** have crafted. The expansion's promise of exploring a new region and delving deeper into **Dandelion**'s backstory taps directly into the community's desire for more of the rich world and complex characters that define **The Witcher 3**.

## What's Next

Beyond the **Songs of the Past** demo, **PAX Australia** boasts a diverse lineup of gaming-related events, including panels with figures from **World of Warcraft** and **Final Fantasy 14**, discussions on game development, and celebrations of tabletop gaming. However, for many, the allure of **The Witcher 3**'s latest chapter will undoubtedly be the main draw, providing a tantalizing preview of Geralt's final adventures.

content_raw: I'm looking forward to an expansion for a game from 2015 more than I am for pretty much any new game coming up. The Songs of the Past add-on for The Witcher 3, which will be out next year, promises to let us explore a whole new region and get to know Dandelion better than ever. I'm more interested in a brand new chunk of world than intimate moments with the bard, but more Witcher 3 is more Witcher 3 even if the focus isn't on everyone's actual favorite character. (Johnny the Godling, of course.) Songs of the Past was shown off at Gamescom, where our Joshua Wolens had a peek and said it looked real good . The rest of us will have to wait for other opportunities, like the one that's been announced as part of the PAX Australia schedule reveal. On Saturday, October 11, attendees will be able to join members of CD Projekt and DLC developer Fool's Theory for a behind-closed-doors live demo of Songs of the Past, and a panel discussion to follow. Other events planned for the three-day event include Storytime with World of Warcraft executive producer Holly Longdale, Final Fantasy 14 veterans Koji Fox and Toshio 'Foxclon' Murouchi suffering through a hot-sauce interview in "A Realm Reburned", and Saros' creative director Gregory Louden talking about a career that's included work on games like Control and Returnal. The tabletop side of gaming will also be well covered with Jasmine 'ThatBronzeGirl' Bhullar, Dungeon Master of the official Dungeons & Dragons liveplay and Dimension 20's Coffin Run, talking about the art of storytelling, and fellow Dimension 20 alumnus Ify Nwadiwe taking part in a D&D one-shot with Deerstalker Pictures . Other guests include composer Mick Gordon and fantasy author Isobelle Carmody. PAX Australia runs from October 9–11 at the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre, and the full schedule is online at the PAX website now.
